body_html:
How to think about it

Heat flows because of a temperature difference. Solids expand by ΔL = αLΔT, and the volume coefficient is about 3α. Water is unusual: it contracts when heated from 0 °C to 4 °C, so lakes freeze from the top. Heat needed to warm a body is mcΔT; to change its state at constant temperature it is mL.

Heat moves by conduction (H = KAΔT/d), convection and radiation. A black body absorbs all radiation; it radiates power ∝ T⁴ (Stefan) and its peak wavelength obeys λmT = 2.9 × 10⁻³ m K (Wien).

Example

2 kg water from 20 °C to 70 °C?

2 × 4186 × 50

Answer: 4.19 × 10⁵ J

Example

Sun at 5800 K. Peak λ?

2.9 × 10⁻³ ÷ 5800

Answer: 500 nm

Common mistakes

  • Adding 273 to temperature differences.
  • Thinking temperature rises while water boils.
  • Using α for volume expansion.
